s1.syndrome_frame: chronic foot pain with soft-tissue nodules and nerve involvement
salient_findings: pain in the plantar aspect of the left foot
three prominent, soft-tissue nodules with swelling and tenderness
numbness in the medial distal plantar foot
key_facts: 19-year-old woman
18-month history of pain in the plantar aspect of her left foot
pain was moderate initially and worsened at night
pain was exacerbated by compression and exposure to cold
three soft-tissue nodules were palpated in the plantar aspect of the left foot
nodules were mobile and not adherent to surrounding tissue
sensation testing revealed numbness in the medial distal plantar foot
toe and foot motor strength were normal
magnetic resonance imaging showed three nodules in the mid-plantar region
lesions were homogeneously isointense to skeletal muscle on T1-weighted images
lesions were homogeneously hyperintense without cystic degeneration on T2-weighted fat-suppressed images

shortlist.label: schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: multiple plexiform schwannoma suspected based on clinical presentation and imaging findings

shortlist.label: glomus tumor

raw.rationale: The clinical presentation of multiple soft-tissue nodules in the plantar aspect of the foot, numbness in the medial distal plantar foot, and the imaging findings of homogeneously isointense to skeletal muscle on T1-weighted images and homogeneously hyperintense without cystic degeneration on T2-weighted fat-suppressed images, are consistent with schwannoma, particularly multiple plexiform schwannoma.

rejected.label: glomus tumor
rejected.why: Glomus tumors are typically smaller, more painful, and have a stronger association with cold-induced pain, which is not the primary complaint in this case.

rejected.label: neurofibroma
rejected.why: Neurofibromas can be multiple, but they are often associated with neurofibromatosis type 1, which the patient denied having a family history of.

rejected.label: nerve sheath myxoma
rejected.why: Nerve sheath myxomas are rare and typically have a more myxoid appearance on imaging, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: perineurioma
rejected.why: Perineuriomas are rare and often have a more infiltrative appearance on imaging, which is not consistent with the well-defined nodules described in this case.
